leading_positions.synthesis: Two members prefer halide perovskites as a stand-alone prize, with the identical trio Miyasaka, Snaith and Park. They share the view that the principle (a defect-tolerant, strongly absorbing semiconductor) is demonstrated and independently reproduced. They also share the same open items: whether Park or Gratzel, Kanatzidis or Seok has the stronger claim to the third place, and whether stability and lead toxicity make a citation premature. Linke would frame the citation around the absorber material and efficiency rather than deployment; Zou's file does not state a citation preference on that point. Each lists B054 as an alternative.

Two members include targeted protein degradation in their preferred configuration, but not the same way or with the same names. Brzezinski proposes a single-part prize to Crews, Deshaies and Handa spanning heterobifunctional degraders and the cereblon glue mechanism. Chabes proposes Crews and Deshaies only, as the second part of a two-part prize and limited to the heterobifunctional concept. Both note that no heterobifunctional degrader is approved and that Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito and others are left out. B054 is also named as an alternative by Aili, Aqvist, Somfai, Linke and Zou, but alternatives are not counted as preferences here.

Two members include base editing, both crediting David R. Liu alone and both as one part of a two-part prize. They differ on the partner: Chabes pairs it with B054, Somfai with B065 (C-N cross-coupling). Both flag the overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Kondo/Nishida priority question, and both acknowledge that omitting Komor and Gaudelli is a cost. Somfai also questions how much chemistry is new, since the deaminase chemistry is known. B069 is an alternative for Aili, Aqvist, Sparr and Brzezinski.

Chabes alone prefers this two-part configuration (Liu for base editing; Crews and Deshaies for degraders). Chabes concedes that two chemical-biology achievements in one prize may be a weaker unit and that naming Komor and Gaudelli would leave no room for the second part.

Somfai alone prefers C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) together with base editing (Liu). He notes that only he ranked B065 in the opening ballots, that it overlaps the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and that the two parts are unrelated and give a weak unifying citation.

Aili prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, citing a clear chemical principle (pKa-tuned lipids) and overwhelming independent confirmation. Aili acknowledges that Hope, MacLachlan and Madden are omitted, that industry did much of the optimisation, and that the 2023 Medicine prize overlaps. Sparr lists B036 as an alternative and says she would reconsider her ranking if the credit could be resolved.

Aqvist prefers first-principles molecular dynamics for Car and Parrinello, citing the cleanest two-person attribution on the list and decades of validation. Aqvist acknowledges that support is thin, that it may read as a methods prize, and that machine-learned potentials, which are not on the shortlist, may eclipse the original method. Linke lists B059 as an alternative while noting the overlap with the 1998 DFT prize.

Sparr prefers biomolecular phase separation for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, framed as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation. Sparr concedes that the in vivo debate continues, that Pappu and Mittag are left out, and that colleagues may see the concept as cell biology rather than chemistry.

areas_of_agreement: No candidate has a stated majority of five: the eight files give two supporters at most for any single ballot, so the committee is dispersed across B017, B036, B044, B054, B059, B065 and B069.
All eight files name three-person (or smaller) cuts and acknowledge that credit is left out for each preferred candidate, so attribution is a live issue for every position.
B054 (targeted protein degradation) is the ballot most often named across the files, as a preference by two members and as an alternative by five more, but its laureates and scope are not agreed.
B069 (base editing) appears as a preference or alternative in six files and always with Liu as laureate, with the same caveat about the 2020 CRISPR prize.
No member discloses a conflict or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether it is new chemistry or protein engineering around known deaminase chemistry (Somfai, Chabes, Aqvist).
Whether the PROTAC concept and the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism are one discovery or two (Brzezinski, Chabes, Aqvist, Zou).
Whether biomolecular condensates are established as a physiological principle or still debated in vivo, and whether they are chemistry or cell biology (Sparr, Linke).
Whether first-principles molecular dynamics is a distinct discovery given the overlap with the 1998 DFT prize and with machine-learned potentials (Aqvist, Linke).
Whether long-range electron transfer through proteins is new relative to Marcus theory (1992), a question Linke put to Brzezinski; B043 is an alternative only for Brzezinski.
attribution_disputes: B017: third laureate beside Miyasaka and Snaith (Park versus Gratzel, Kanatzidis or Seok), a cut Linke and Zou both propose but both say is contestable.
B054: Brzezinski proposes Crews, Deshaies and Handa; Chabes proposes Crews and Deshaies only; Ciulli, Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim are left out in either case.
B069: Liu alone (Chabes, Somfai) versus including Komor and Gaudelli, and the Kondo/Nishida priority for cytidine deamination.
B036: Cullis, Anderson and Langer (Aili) versus Hope, MacLachlan and Madden, with industrial formulators also relevant; Aili has not verified priority records.
B044: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag, and the split between experiment and theory.
B065: whether Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling should be credited with Buchwald and Hartwig.
maturity_disputes: B054: no heterobifunctional degrader is approved; members differ on whether late-stage trial evidence is sufficient or approval should come first.
B017: operational stability and lead toxicity are unresolved; Linke and Zou differ in how much weight to give this relative to the demonstrated absorber discovery.
B069: the long-term safety record (bystander edits, RNA off-target deamination) is short.
B044: debate continues about which condensates are phase-separated in vivo and what function this serves.
questions_for_round2: For B054, should the citation rest on the heterobifunctional PROTAC concept, the cereblon glue mechanism, or both, and who are the three laureates (Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Sakamoto)? Does the absence of an approved PROTAC drug delay recognition?

For B017, does Park or Gratzel, Kanatzidis or Seok merit the third place with Miyasaka and Snaith, and can the citation be written around the absorber and efficiency without relying on stability or deployment?
For B069, is base editing a distinct discovery after the 2020 CRISPR prize, and should the citation name Liu alone, or Komor and Gaudelli, or Kondo and Nishida, at the cost of a second part?
Is a two-part prize (Chabes: B069 with B054; Somfai: B065 with B069) coherent, or does the committee prefer a single-part prize, and which pairing, if any, can five members support?
What is the decisive, separable step and its owner in B036 (ionizable lipid design) and does the 2023 Medicine prize close the room for a delivery-chemistry citation?

For B044 and B059, can supporters state the narrow discovery to be cited (condensates as a principle; first-principles MD beyond the 1998 DFT prize and machine-learned potentials) so the committee can compare them with the broader-supported candidates?
Which members who listed alternatives would move to a preferred position, and for which ballot, given the dispersion across seven ballots without any five-member majority?
summary.chair_observation: On the round-1 files alone, preferences are dispersed: at most two members explicitly prefer any single ballot (B017, B054 and B069 each have two), and no configuration has five. B054 and B069 are most widely named once alternatives are counted, but with unresolved differences in laureates and scope, and B017 is the only ballot with an identical laureate trio proposed by two members. Every member acknowledges significant omitted credit, so round 2 turns on attribution and citation wording more than on whether the underlying science is established. I am a supporter of B017 and have tried to represent the other positions on their own terms.
